title: Keyset pagination with a limit-plus-one probe
source: Authored for the CodeReview benchmark corpus (expanded clean stratum), 2026-11-05
false_flag_note: A reviewer may flag 'LIMIT limit + 1' as an off-by-one bug and the discarded row as waste. Fetching one row past the page is the standard probe: has_more is exactly 'a (limit+1)-th row exists', the page is sliced back to limit before returning, and next_cursor is the id of the last row actually returned, so the next page resumes strictly after it (WHERE id > cursor) with no overlap or gap. The limit is clamped to [1, 100] and the cursor is parsed defensively.
